text:
devon: Morning passback — quick summary of overnight work and current risks. We had a series of 429 spikes for short queries routed to eu-west yesterday 03:10–04:00 UTC. Most traffic recovered after throttling the small-model pool, but we still see periodic elevated p95 on relay paths.

anya: TL;DR of what was done: autoscaler temporary cap applied to small-model pool, KV cache leader rebalance kicked, and we disabled burst routing to the fallback cheap-host pool. That reduced amplification but didn't fully remove the p95 tail.

kai: Current status: customer impact is limited to <0.2% of requests; we have no ongoing pages. Observability notes: bursty prefix loads correlated with a new batch job from internal-search that started around 02:55 UTC.

miguel: Actions for night shift (done): 1) Applied autoscaler max=30 for small-models. 2) Manually rebalanced KV leaders across nodes 5/6/7. 3) Added quick rule to route heavy embedding requests off eu-west to us-east for 30m window.

oncall-bot: Incident note created — INC-2026-3327 — severity: low. PagerDuty alert group: embed-p95. Link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-3327

devon: Handoff checklist for today: 1) Primary = anya, Secondary = kai. 2) Watch for any regressions in prefix hit-rates (esp /search/*). 3) Keep KV eviction rate <0.5%/min. 4) If p95 > 800ms for 10m, escalate to infra-oncall.

anya: I'm primary for the next 12h. Kai you're secondary — if I'm in a meeting ping me and take the bridge. Bridge link: https://redwood.zoom.us/j/9876543210 

kai: Got it. I can take the bridge if page or if devon asks. Quick note — set me as secondary in PD for the next 8h.

miguel: Runbook pointers: KV leader imbalance playbook https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-leader-imbalance (steps we used), autoscaler tuning doc https://redwood.internal/runbooks/autoscaler-emergency. Also saved diagnostics to the incident folder: /srv/incidents/INC-2026-3327/logs.tar.gz

devon: Diagnostic snippets that helped: 
```
# quick check for eviction storm
kubectl -n inference exec -it monitor -- curl -s http://kv-metrics.local/evictions | jq .rate
# query prefix heatmap
python tools/heatmap.py --window 10m --prefix /search
```

anya: Ongoing items (next steps): 1) Confirm internal-search batch job owner and request a staggered window. 2) Run a targeted QoS test against a representative /search/ prefix to validate latency under autoscaler cap. 3) If p95 doesn't drop to <400ms within 2 hours, consider rolling a slightly more quantized small-model variant for eu-west.

kai: Coverage gaps to note — EU nights have only one infra responder. If we see multi-region fallout we need to call in oncall-eu-sre. I've added a temporary rule in routing to prefer steady pools; keep an eye on errors after route change.

devon: Risk register entry (quick): potential regression from routing rule rollback, risk: medium, mitigation: can revert routing via canary release in <=5m. Revert play: go to Console -> Routing -> Policy -> rollback last change.

sre-runbooks-bot: Quick link dump: Runbooks referenced: [KV leader imbalance], [Autoscaler emergency], [Routing rollback]. Also posted checklist to the runbooks channel.

anya: For the handoff note I'll attach a short checklist in the incident ticket and mark items "in-progress" vs "complete". Anyone taking PM followups? I can coordinate with internal-search.

miguel: I'll own contacting internal-search and request they split their batch into 4 smaller windows. I'll post update here once they've agreed.

kai: Before I sign off to focus on deploys, quick smoke: can someone run `curl -I https://eu-west.api.redwood.ai/health` every 10m for the next hour and paste headers? I want to see proxy latency headers.

devon: I'll add that check to the synthetic monitor and ping results into this thread.

anya: Final passback items for whoever picks up next: - Primary/Secondary noted above. - Links: incident, runbooks, bridge. - Watchers: infra-oncall, internal-search oncall. - Escalation threshold: p95 > 800ms for 10 min. - Backout plan: rollback routing change (Console).

devon: Thanks team. If anything spikes call the bridge immediately and @kai if I'm in a meeting. :thumbsup:
